answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a vault before it may submit bids, with voting weight capped by the amount and duration of the lock. Creating a thousand aliases then does not create a thousand units of influence: the attacker must acquire and immobilize proportionally more capital, paying opportunity cost and risking slashing if fraud is proven. This makes a velvet swarm of cheap accounts costly rather than powerful; the fable of multiplying names no longer bypasses the resource bound.
